stem: Polonium-193 (¹⁹³₈₄Po) is an unstable nuclide. A nucleus of polonium-193 decays to a nucleus of lead-189 (¹⁸⁹₈₂Pb) by emitting an alpha-particle.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead:
Radioactive decay is both random and spontaneous.

State what is meant by:

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Data for the binding energy per nucleon of the particles involved in the decay of a nucleus of polonium-193 are given in Table 9.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Determine the energy, in eV, released when a nucleus of polonium-193 decays into a nucleus of lead-189.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead:
A pure sample of polonium-193 contains *N*₀ nuclei. After a time *t* the sample contains *N* nuclei of polonium-193. The variation of ln (*N*/*N*₀) with *t* is shown in Fig. 9.1.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: State the name of the quantity that is represented by the magnitude of the gradient of the line in Fig. 9.1.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use Fig. 9.1 to determine the half-life, in ms, of polonium-193.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.lead: Positron emission tomography (PET scanning) uses a radioactive tracer.
parts.text: State what happens to the positrons emitted by the tracer.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why a tracer with a half-life of approximately 2 hours is a suitable tracer to use.
